newsitem.title: UK: Lower UK wheat quality may cut prices, HGCA says.
newsitem.headline: Lower UK wheat quality may cut prices, HGCA says.

text.p: The reduced quality of wheat from the UK's 1996 crop could force prices lower to maintain its competitive position, according to the UK Home Grown Cereals Authority's Weekly Digest, issued on Monday.
In the report, the HGCA said that Group 2 UK wheat varieties recorded an average 10.7 percent preotein in 1996, against 11.4 percent a year earlier.
"This means that UK wheat prices may on average have to fall further below EU (European Union) values this year to maintain competitiveness," the HGCA said.
However, the authority noted that certain types of wheat and poor samples were excluded from surveys in France, Germany and other EU member states.
Improved wheat crops and better quality in Spain and Italy were likely to hit UK wheat exports in the two most important markets, the HGCA said.
The increasing importance of feed and lower grade milling wheats on the continent may help even out the quality difference between UK and other EU wheat, the HGCA said.
It will also boost average yields. Indeed, the change partly contributed to this year's record EU crop.
"Given the reduced set-aside area and assuming a continuation of the trend towards more feed and lower grade milling wheats, another bumper EU wheat harvest seems likely next year," the HGCA said.
